func evaluateAudit(facts auditFacts) []Result {
	results := []Result{
		auditExposure(facts),
		auditFirewallResult(facts),
		auditIPForward(facts),
		auditSSHRootLogin(facts),
		auditSSHPassword(facts),
		auditAuthorizedKeys(facts),
		auditUID0(facts),
		auditEmptyPasswords(facts),
		auditSudo(facts),
		auditRootGroups(facts),
		auditSensitiveModes(facts),
		auditPath(facts),
		auditKernelSysctl(facts),
		auditReboot(facts),
	}
	if facts.Container != "" {
		results = append(results, auditPrivileged(facts), auditDockerSocket(facts), auditRootUser(facts), auditHostNamespace(facts))
	}
	return results
}

/*
 * BPF_CORE_READ() is used to simplify BPF CO-RE relocatable read, especially
 * when there are few pointer chasing steps.
 * E.g., what in non-BPF world (or in BPF w/ BCC) would be something like:
 *	int x = s->a.b.c->d.e->f->g;
 * can be succinctly achieved using BPF_CORE_READ as:
 *	int x = BPF_CORE_READ(s, a.b.c, d.e, f, g);
 *
 * BPF_CORE_READ will decompose above statement into 4 bpf_core_read (BPF
 * CO-RE relocatable bpf_probe_read_kernel() wrapper) calls, logically
 * equivalent to:
 * 1. const void *__t = s->a.b.c;
 * 2. __t = __t->d.e;
 * 3. __t = __t->f;
 * 4. return __t->g;
 *
 * Equivalence is logical, because there is a heavy type casting/preservation
 * involved, as well as all the reads are happening through
 * bpf_probe_read_kernel() calls using __builtin_preserve_access_index() to
 * emit CO-RE relocations.
 *
 * N.B. Only up to 9 "field accessors" are supported, which should be more
 * than enough for any practical purpose.
 */
#define BPF_CORE_READ(src, a, ...) ({					    \
	___type((src), a, ##__VA_ARGS__) __r;				    \
	BPF_CORE_READ_INTO(&__r, (src), a, ##__VA_ARGS__);		    \

#define BPF_PROBE_READ_USER(src, a, ...) ({				    \
	___type((src), a, ##__VA_ARGS__) __r;				    \
	BPF_PROBE_READ_USER_INTO(&__r, (src), a, ##__VA_ARGS__);	    \
	__r;								    \
})

# exits.yaml은 로그인마다 바뀌지 않는 로컬 파일이라, remote group처럼 edc를 부르지 않고 grep으로
# 이름만 뽑는다. .edc/exits.yaml을 cwd/exits.yaml보다 먼저 본다(discoverRemoteFile과 같은 순서).
_edc_route_exits() {
  local -a exits
  local file
  for file in .edc/exits.yaml exits.yaml; do
    [[ -f $file ]] || continue
    exits=(${(f)"$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*-?[[:space:]]*name:' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*name:[[:space:]]*//')"})
    break
  done
  (( ${#exits} )) && _describe -t exits 'exit name' exits
}

const bashCompletion = `# edc completion bash 출력. source <(edc completion bash)로 읽는다.

# exits.yaml은 로컬 파일이므로 remote group의 edc 왕복 대신 grep으로 이름만 뽑는다.
# .edc/exits.yaml을 exits.yaml보다 먼저 본다(discoverRemoteFile과 같은 순서).
_edc_route_exit_names() {
  local file
  for file in .edc/exits.yaml exits.yaml; do
    if [[ -f $file ]]; then
      grep -E '^[[:space:]]*-?[[:space:]]*name:' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*name:[[:space:]]*//'
      return
    fi
  done
}

_edc() {
  local cur prev command index
  cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
  prev="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}"
  local commands="@@COMMANDS@@"
  local common="--timeout --json --verbose -v --redact"
  if [[ $COMP_CWORD -eq 1 ]]; then
    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "$commands" -- "$cur"))
    return
  fi
  command="${COMP_WORDS[1]}"
  case "$command" in
    top)
      case "$prev" in
        --json) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f -- "$cur")); return ;;
        -w|--write) if [[ $cur != -* ]]; then COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f -- "$cur")); return; fi ;;
        --split) if [[ $cur != -* ]]; then COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "all none cpu mem disk net psi" -- "$cur")); return; fi ;;
        --interface) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "all physical $(ls /sys/class/net 2>/dev/null)" -- "$cur")); return ;;

return
      fi
      if [[ ${COMP_WORDS[2]} == history ]]; then
        for ((index=3; index<COMP_CWORD; index++)); do
          case "${COMP_WORDS[index]}" in
            --dir|--file|--key|--limit|--command|--json|-dir|-file|-key|-limit|-command|-json) ((index++)) ;;
            --) COMPREPLY=(); if [[ $index -eq $((COMP_CWORD-1)) ]]; then COMPREPLY=($(compgen -c -- "$cur")); fi; return ;;
            -|[!-]*) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f -- "$cur")); return ;;
          esac
        done
        case "$prev" in
          --dir|--file|--json) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f -- "$cur")); return ;;
          --key|--limit) COMPREPLY=(); return ;;
          --command) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -c -- "$cur")); return ;;
        esac
        if [[ $cur == -* ]]; then
          COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "--dir --file --key --command --limit --failed --follow --json --" -- "$cur"))
        else
          COMPREPLY=($(compgen -c -- "$cur"))
        fi
        return
      fi
      for ((index=2; index<COMP_CWORD; index++)); do
        if [[ ${COMP_WORDS[index]} == -- ]]; then
          COMPREPLY=()
          if [[ $index -eq $((COMP_CWORD-1)) ]]; then COMPREPLY=($(compgen -c -- "$cur")); fi
          return
        fi
      done
      case "$prev" in
        --stream) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "stdout stderr" -- "$cur")); return ;;
        --command-display) COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "full name none" -- "$cur")); return ;;

func mergeConfigSection[T any](existing, fallback T) T {
	baseData, _ := yaml.Marshal(fallback)
	overlayData, _ := yaml.Marshal(existing)
	var baseNode, overlayNode yaml.Node
	_ = yaml.Unmarshal(baseData, &baseNode)
	_ = yaml.Unmarshal(overlayData, &overlayNode)
	mergeYAMLMapping(baseNode.Content[0], overlayNode.Content[0])
	mergedData, _ := yaml.Marshal(baseNode.Content[0])
	var merged T
	_ = yaml.Unmarshal(mergedData, &merged)
	return merged
}

func runInfo(args []string, version string) int {
	set := newFlagSet("info")
	set.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
	config := activeConfig.Defaults.Info
	includePublic := set.Bool("public", configuredBool(config.Public, true), T("command.info.option.public"))
	timeout := set.Duration("timeout", configuredDurationFallback(config.Timeout, activeConfig.Defaults.Common.Timeout, 3*time.Second), T("command.info.option.timeout"))
	verbose := configuredBoolFallback(config.Verbose, activeConfig.Defaults.Common.Verbose, false)
	set.BoolVar(&verbose, "verbose", verbose, T("command.info.option.verbose"))
	set.BoolVar(&verbose, "v", verbose, T("option.verbose"))
	if err := set.Parse(args); err != nil {
		return 2
	}
	if set.NArg() != 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, T("cli.usage", "edc info [--public=false] [--timeout 3s] [-v]"))
		return 2
	}
	// 수집기는 서로 의존하지 않는다. 공인 IP 조회와 python shim 확인은 각각 수백 ms가 걸리므로 순서대로 돌리면 시간이 더해진다.
	var (
		collectors                                            sync.WaitGroup
		details                                               hostDetails
		hostErr, interfaceErr, diskErr, memoryErr, processErr error
		interfaces                                            []interfaceDetails
		disks                                                 []diskDetails
		memory                                                infoMemory
		processes                                             []topProcess
		capabilities                                          []infoCapability
		listen                                                Result
		health                                                *networkHealth
		public                                                *publicNetworkInfo
		publicErr, publicIPErr                                error
		publicIP, pythonVersion                               string
		signals                                               infoSignals

  usage_label: "usage"
  usage: "edc <command> [options] [target]"
  common_label: "common"
  detail_label: "detail"
  help_command_summary: "Show the command list"
  detail_hint: "edc help <command>"
  options_label: "options"
  common_options_label: "common options"
  examples_label: "examples"
  group:
    diagnose: "diagnose"
    observe: "observe"
    host: "host changes"
    record: "record and remote"
    tool: "tools"

option:
  timeout: "run time limit"
  json: "JSON output path, - for stdout"
  verbose: "print the detailed evidence"
  redact: "hide sensitive values in output"

command:
  doctor:
    summary: "Check DNS, TCP, TLS, and HTTP at once"
    option:
      profile: "full adds bandwidth and responsiveness"
      all_ips: "check each DNS IP and look up its ASN holder"

notes:
      - "edc runs nine probes together and prints them in one format."
      - "In a terminal, each probe keeps one line and updates it."
      - "Press Ctrl-C to cancel. edc returns exit code 4."
  dns:
    summary: "Name lookup and resolver setup"
    sub:
      lookup: "addresses that the system resolver returns"
      compare: "system DNS against 1.1.1.1 or --resolver"
      config: "resolver settings of this host"
    option:
      resolver: "compare against this DNS server; repeat for more"
    notes:
      - "lookup reads addresses; compare checks system DNS against other resolvers."
      - "compare uses 1.1.1.1 unless --resolver is given."
  tcp:
    summary: "TCP connection check"
    notes:
      - "A failure keeps the phase and the cause, and returns exit code 1."
  tls:
    summary: "Certificate and handshake check"
    option:
      min_days: "a shorter remaining life than N is a failure"
    notes:
      - "Less than 30 days is a warning. --min-days makes an earlier expiry a failure."
  http:
    summary: "HTTP response check"
    option:
      expect_status: "a different status code is a failure"
      header: "add a request header; repeat for more"
      body: "save the last response body; - writes it to stdout"
    notes:

- "A 4xx response is a warning. A 5xx response is a failure."
      - "With redirects, edc lists each request: status, URL, timings, and peer."
      - "-v adds the headers of each response and the start of the body."
      - "edc hides the values of Authorization, Cookie, and similar headers."
      - "--body - writes the body to stdout and the result to stderr."
  audit:
    summary: "Read-only check of host exposure and settings (Linux)"
    notes:
      - "It reads files, sysctl values, and listening sockets."
      - "It changes nothing and sends nothing over the network."
      - "Run it as root. Without root, some checks show skip."
      - "The firewall check sees this host only, not a cloud security group."
      - "It does not match package versions against CVEs."
  changes:
    summary: "Recent package, /etc, and service changes (Linux)"
    notes:
      - "It reads dpkg, dnf, and yum logs, /etc mtimes, and systemd unit state."
      - "It changes nothing and sends nothing over the network."
      - "Each service shows only its latest start and its restart count."
      - "For /etc, it reports the file mtime only, not the content."
      - "It does not read compressed logs, it warns about them."
    option:
      since: "how far back to look, a Go duration such as 24h or 90m"
      verbose: "show every change, not only the newest 50"
  check:
    summary: "Scan for what is broken now (Linux and macOS)"
    option:
      routine: "run a routine from [check.routines] in config.toml"
      group: "run check on each host of an edc remote group"
      inventory: "inventory file for --group"
    notes:
      - "It checks services, processes, memory, disks, the kernel log, time, network, containers, file handles, and reboot."

- "The built-in checks change nothing and send nothing over the network."
      - "Each finding names the edc command that shows more."
      - "Without root, some checks show skip, not pass."
      - "macOS reads launchd, memory pressure, disks, network, containers, file handles, diagnostic reports, thermal pressure, and Time Machine. time and reboot show skip."
      - "--group runs edc check on each host over SSH. Each host needs an edc that has check."
      - "A routine adds unit rules, limits, and shell commands from config.toml. A command passes when it exits with 0."
  events:
    summary: "Kernel, systemd, and macOS jetsam and panic signals in time order"
    option:
      since: "how far back to read, such as 30m or 48h"
    notes:
      - "On Linux, it reads the kernel log and the systemd journal."
      - "Run it as root or as a member of adm or systemd-journal."
      - "Without that access, the checks show skip, not pass."
      - "On macOS, it reads jetsam and panic reports in /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports."
  net:
    summary: "Interfaces, route, ping, and trace"
    sub:
      interfaces: "network interfaces and their addresses"
      route: "the interface and gateway toward a host"
      ping: "ping a host"
      trace: "the path to a host, with traceroute or tracepath"
  route:
    summary: "Check, switch, and roll back the default route on a gateway VM"
    sub:
      check: "inspect the current state, change nothing"
      switch: "switch with a rollback timer, then verify"
      status: "show a pending or finished switch"
      rollback: "restore one state file"
    notes:
      - "This command runs locally on the gateway VM whose route it changes."
      - "switch and rollback need root. edc does not add sudo itself."

- "check never changes a route. switch arms a rollback timer first."
      - "status reads /run/edc. rollback --state repeats one state file."
  disk:
    summary: "Grow a partition and file system after a disk resize"
    sub:
      check: "show the mounts that can grow, change nothing"
      grow: "grow a partition and its file system"
    notes:
      - "check reads the layers and changes nothing."
      - "Run check as root to see the size of every layer."
      - "grow needs root. edc does not add sudo itself."
      - "grow cannot be undone. Take a snapshot of the volume first."
  change:
    summary: "Protected host changes with automatic rollback"
    sub:
      apply: "apply, then roll back unless confirmed"
      status: "pending changes and their remaining time"
      confirm: "keep a change, stop its rollback timer"
      rollback: "restore the state from before apply"
  top:
    summary: "Live resource dashboard"
    option:
      interval: "time between samples"
      count: "rows to print, 0 runs until you quit"
      no_header: "drop the host and column header"
      process: "match PIDs or command names, comma-separated"
      top: "top processes in each JSON line without --process, 0 for none"
      sort: "order of --top: cpu or mem"
      full: "match and show the full command line"
      split: "one box each for cpu, mem, disk, net, psi, default all"
      view: "first view, such as network or split"
      panels: "panels under the table: cpu,mem,disk,net,psi,ai,events"

columns: "all-view column groups, + shows more: net+,cpu,mem"
      interface: "net values add only these: names, globs, physical, all"
      detail: "CPU wait, I/O latency (Linux eBPF, root); macOS CPU wait"
      ebpf: "same as --detail"
      write: "append to SQLite; omit path for the default DB"
      auto_record: "record load, swap out, or memory pressure spikes"
      retain: "while recording, delete top runs idle longer than this (30d, 2w)"
      json: "one JSON line for each sample, - for stdout"
    notes:
      - "Press w to start/stop DB recording. Each restart creates a new run; p pauses recording too."
      - "In a terminal, edc opens a dashboard. q quits, p pauses, +/- moves the interval."
      - "--count, --json, a pipe, or NO_COLOR gives the table instead."
      - "With --process, it opens the process view. 1 shows host columns, f returns."
      - "f follows a signal: its view, then the busiest process. / filters, Esc clears."
      - "edc top setup picks the view, boxes, and panels with a live preview."
  watch:
    summary: "Observe HTTP or file changes and run explicit file actions"
    sub:
      http: "request a URL again and again until Ctrl-C"
      fs: "watch file changes, optionally run a command"
    option:
      interval: "seconds between samples (minimum 0.1)"
      duration: "stop after this time; omit to run until Ctrl-C"
    notes:
      - "Use watch http for HTTP checks; the previous watch URL form remains supported."
      - "watch fs observes the current directory by default."
      - "File events are create,modify,remove,rename; reading a file is not observed."
      - "--exec or --rules enables command execution."
  info:
    summary: "System, network, and disk information"
    option:
      public: "skip the public IP lookup (DNS; ipinfo.io with -v)"

timeout: "time limit of the public lookup"
      verbose: "print the cause of a failed lookup"
    notes:
      - "edc asks for the public IP by default and drops the line after the time limit."
      - "Disk usage is the total size minus the available space."
  view:
    summary: "Read a log with color and follow it as it grows"
    option:
      lines: "last N lines; the screen keeps N lines (default 10,000)"
      follow: "in a pipe, follow the file like tail -F; the screen always follows"
    notes:
      - "In a terminal, it opens a screen at the end of the file and follows new lines."
      - "Up or PgUp stops the list, and the header counts the new lines. End, l, or Esc follows again."
      - "In an access log, the list shows time, status, method, bytes, and path. A host, client, or date that is the same on every kept line is hidden and named in the header. c shows the raw lines, and ← → scroll the list sideways."
      - "It reads nginx and Apache access logs, JSON lines, and lines with a level such as ERROR or WARN."
      - "The stats panel counts status classes or levels, top paths and clients, and the last error."
      - "The stats count only the lines that the screen keeps. i hides the panel."
      - "The panel sits on the right in 120 columns or more, and below the list otherwise."
      - "Enter shows the fields and the whole line, with the stack trace lines below it."
      - "When the file is rotated or truncated, it marks the place and reads the new file from the start."
      - "In a pipe or with NO_COLOR, it writes the bytes unchanged, like cat. -f follows like tail -F."
      - "edc alias prints short aliases such as ev, evn, and evf."
  grep:
    summary: "Search logs, code, and file paths"
    option:
      model_clear: "remove the shared model and runtime"
      semantic_yes: "confirm the model download without a prompt"
      ask_keyword: "use keyword ranking with --ask without a model"
      semantic_init: "build or rebuild the local semantic index"
      semantic_status: "show semantic index metadata"
      semantic_files: "indexed and total chunks for each file"
      semantic_clear: "remove the semantic index"

semantic: "search code with the initialized local embedding index (implies --ask)"
      ask: "search code by meaning with a local embedding index"
      ask_json: "emit JSON for --ask"
      ask_limit: "maximum --ask results (default 10, max 100)"
      code: "search code contents with .gitignore rules"
      paths: "search file paths instead of file contents"
      hidden: "include hidden files in code or path searches"
      no_ignore: "do not apply .gitignore rules"
      ignore_case: "ignore case"
      regex: "the pattern is a regular expression (default: plain text)"
      numbers: "show line numbers"
      files: "list only the files with a match"
      context: "show N lines around each match"
      level: "lines at this level or above: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal"
      status: "HTTP status codes: 5xx, 404, 500-503, separated by commas"
      since: "lines at or after this time: 10m, 2h, 1d, 2026-10-27 09:00, 09:00"
      until: "lines at or before this time"
      ordered: "the log is in time order: --since bisects the file and skips files that end before the time"
      index: "build the index now, or never use one (default: build on the second search within 24h)"
      jobs: "goroutines that build the index (default: half the CPUs, at most 4; limit 64)"
      verify: "compare the index result with a whole read and remove a wrong index"
      last: "the newest N matches, read from the end of the file"
    notes:
      - "Semantic search runs locally. --semantic-init downloads the English MiniLM model and runtime with your confirmation."
      - "The index is stored in the user cache, not the project. Files that change are re-embedded on the next semantic query."
      - "--ask --keyword uses local keyword ranking; it does not understand meaning or generate answers. Both modes skip binary, invalid UTF-8 and files larger than 2 MiB."
      - "With a terminal and one pattern, grep searches code in the current directory. Pipes read stdin; an explicit path keeps log search behavior."
      - "Code and path searches default to the current directory and skip hidden files and .git; --hidden includes hidden files, --no-ignore ignores .gitignore."
      - "Code search reads current files without a log index and prints line numbers."
      - "A directory is searched recursively. Binary files are skipped, and .gz files are read in order."
      - "The output matches grep: the path appears with several files, the line number with -n, and -C adds context lines."
      - "--since and --until filter lines by their timestamps. With --ordered, --since bisects a file in time order and skips files that end before the time, so a recent window reads a few MB of a multi-GB log. edc checks the order at 16 points only, so lines in an out-of-order stretch between those points can be skipped. Leave out --ordered for a log that mixes sources or has clock jumps."

- "--last reads the file from the end and stops after N matches."
      - "With --level, --status, --since, or --until, the pattern can be left out when the first argument is an existing file or directory."
      - "Lines of a stack trace carry the level and time of their ERROR line, so --level error returns the trace too."
      - "edc alias prints short aliases such as eg, egs, and ege."
      - "Files of 64 MB or more get an index in the cache directory on the second search within 24h. It records which 1 MB blocks hold which letters, times, levels, and statuses, so later searches read only the blocks that can match. The index assumes a log that only grows: a file edited in place keeps its index until it shrinks or its first or last indexed block changes, so use --no-index or --verify-index for such a file."
      - "Every search tells on stderr whether it used, built, or skipped the index, when stderr is a terminal."
      - "In a pipe or with NO_COLOR, the bytes of a line stay unchanged. Exit codes: 0 found, 1 none, 2 error."
  search:
    summary: "Search code by meaning with the local semantic engine"
    option:
      limit: "maximum results, from 1 to 100"
      json: "emit one versioned JSON document"
      yes: "authorize the first model download without a prompt"
    notes:
      - "edc search accepts a natural-language query followed by zero or more files or directories."
      - "The first positional argument is the complete quoted query; every following positional argument is a path. Use -- when a query or path begins with a dash."
      - "It shares the local MiniLM index with edc grep --ask and never calls a cloud service after model installation."
  du:
    summary: "Disk usage under a directory, largest first (Linux and macOS)"
    option:
      top: "rows to show, the default fits the terminal"
      workers: "directories to read at the same time"
      cross_mounts: "count the mounts below the path too"
      no_browse: "show progress and bars, then exit"
      refresh: "refresh the browse screen: auto, 0 (off), or an interval such as 10s"
      timeout: "time limit, after it edc shows what it counted"
      verbose: "show every unreadable directory and skipped mount"
    notes:
      - "It reads only. It changes and deletes nothing."
      - "It counts disk blocks as du does. A hard link counts once."
      - "It stays on one file system and lists the mounts that it skipped."
      - "A bind or overlay mount shares a file system, so its size shows as -."

- "On Linux, it also shows deleted files that a process still holds open."
      - "In a terminal, it opens a screen to browse. q prints the result."
      - "On Linux, docker storage paths also show container names."
      - "On macOS, APFS shared blocks and snapshots prevent a not found comparison."
      - "On the browse screen, edc reads again the directories that changed. The interval is 5s or more and keeps the cost under 2%."
      - "It also checks the size of the large files on the screen. A small file that grows in place shows only after r."
      - "r reads the open directory again, a turns the refresh off or on. A network file system starts with the refresh off."
      - "--refresh works only on the browse screen. The output on q is the tree at that time."
  clean:
    summary: "Disk usage of known dev caches, read only (Linux and macOS)"
    option:
      progress: "show timed progress on stderr; --progress=false disables it"
      workers: "parallel directories per size scan"
      timeout: "time limit, after it edc marks the rest not scanned"
      project: "root to search for marked build folders, repeat for more"
      group: "run clean on each host of an edc remote group"
      inventory: "inventory file for --group"
      verbose: "show every candidate, more groups, reasons, cleanup commands"
    notes:
      - "It reads only. It changes and deletes nothing."
      - "Interactive terminals show an inline progress board; q/Esc stops, ? shows help. NO_COLOR or TERM=dumb uses plain logs. --progress enables JSON stderr logs; --progress=false disables progress."
      - "Workers apply to each directory size scan, including --project build folders; default 4, configurable with defaults.du.workers."
      - "Candidate discovery and scan sections stay sequential. Worktree git checks run up to min(workers, 4) at a time."
      - "It measures tool caches, browsers, Xcode data, app caches, logs, and models."
      - "It shows usage. Only the Docker engine reports what a cleanup can free."
      - "APFS clones, snapshots, and hard links can make a sum larger."
      - "A missing tool or a failed check shows a status, never 0 B."
      - "It reads Docker by socket, the OrbStack disk, and worktrees. None is summed."
      - "It lists what it does not measure. -v shows why."
  where:
    summary: "The near region and the shape of this network"
    option:

provider: "providers to measure: all, aws, gcp"
      count: "measurements for each region"
    notes:
      - "edc opens a TCP handshake to a public endpoint and closes it."
      - "It sends no request and reads no body."
      - "edc resolves each name once, so the DNS time stays out of the distance."
      - "It also reports the public IP, the ASN, the Cloudflare PoP, NAT, and a tunnel."
      - "Addresses are visible by default. --redact hides them in screen and JSON output."
      - "In a terminal, a progress line counts the regions. Press q to cancel."
      - "-v opens every provider row."
  listen:
    summary: "Sockets that wait for a connection"
    option:
      tcp: "show TCP sockets only"
      udp: "show bound UDP sockets only"
      unix: "show unix domain sockets only"
      all: "show TCP, UDP and unix domain sockets"
      watch: "show ports opening and closing until interrupted"
      verbose: "add the account, the descriptor and the queue columns"
      full: "show the working directory and the command line below each row"
    notes:
      - "It shows TCP LISTEN sockets and bound UDP sockets."
      - "A family flag is a filter. --tcp keeps TCP and drops the rest."
      - "Two flags keep both. --all adds unix domain sockets."
      - "A unix socket has a path, not a port. The port column shows -."
      - "It skips connected sockets."
      - "-v adds the account, the file descriptor and the queue."
      - "The queue is Recv-Q/Send-Q. For a TCP listener it is the accept queue."
      - "-v adds columns only. The rows stay the same."
      - "--full adds a gray line below each row: the working directory and the command line."
      - "For node, python, ruby, perl and php, the line starts with the script name."
      - "Values of options such as --password and --token and URL passwords show as ***."

- "With --json, edc listen includes args and cwd when edc can read them. --full does not work with --watch."
  svc:
    summary: "systemd services, or one service on one screen (Linux)"
    notes:
      - "Without a unit, it lists the services. Failed ones come first."
      - "In a terminal, Enter opens one service and Esc goes back."
      - "It shows state, uptime, restarts, processes, fds, sockets, and journal errors."
      - "It reads only. It does not start, stop, or reload the unit."
      - "It needs Linux with systemd. On other hosts it shows skip."
      - "Run it as root. Without root, fds, socket owners, and the journal show skip."
    option:
      all: "also list the services that are not running"
  ctr:
    summary: "Docker containers over a Unix socket (Linux, macOS)"
    notes:
      - "Without a container, it lists containers. Failed containers come first."
      - "In a terminal, Enter opens one container and Esc returns to the list."
      - "It reads container state, health, image, process, limits, and logs."
      - "It uses the Docker Engine API. It does not call Docker CLI."
      - "Set DOCKER_HOST to an absolute Unix socket URL to select a socket."
      - "Set DOCKER_CONTEXT=default to ignore DOCKER_HOST. Other contexts are unsupported."
      - "The API does not expose file descriptors, actual listeners, log size, or cumulative OOM kills."
      - "Missing API data shows an unavailable reason."
    option:
      all: "also list the containers that exited with code 0"
      collector_image: "run a local Linux collector image for extra metrics on detail requests"
  quality:
    summary: "Network responsiveness (RPM) and throughput"
    option:
      server: "responsiveness config URL"
    notes:
      - "macOS runs networkQuality. Other systems measure natively."

- "The native test follows the IETF responsiveness draft."
      - "--server sets the config URL. Apple's mensura server is the default."
      - "The measurement needs tens of seconds."
      - "The timeout is 30s. defaults.quality.timeout overrides it."
      - "defaults.common.timeout does not apply. The native test runs to the limit."
  capture:
    summary: "Packet capture (Linux and macOS)"
    option:
      mode: "capture mode: pcap or events"
      interface: "interface to capture (required)"
      duration: "capture time, 60s at most"
      count: "packets, 10000 at most"
      filter: "BPF filter"
      output: "pcap output path"
      yes: "skip the question"
    notes:
      - "This task needs a privilege. edc shows the plan and asks before it starts."
      - "A PCAP file can hold credentials and personal data."
      - "The JSON redaction does not apply to the PCAP payload."
  trace:
    summary: "Trace network, I/O, socket, drop, sched, process, syscall, and CPU"
    option:
      duration: "trace time, max 60s. Omit for Ctrl-C"
      slow: "min latency, e.g. 20us, 250ms. Default io/sched 1ms"
      raw: "print raw event JSONL"
      live: "compatibility flag. Trace is live by default"
      group_by: "group by source, target, port, process, event, path"
      process: "match PIDs or command names, comma-separated"
      destination: "filter by destination host and port"
      detail: "list each connection or flow in the summary"
      yes: "skip the question"
      side: "http and database traces: both sides. dns: client"

payload: "http, socket: first 4 KiB. =all: up to 1 MiB"
      show_secrets: "http: masked headers. databases: SQL, values"
      tls: "http: HTTPS plaintext. Auto by default. =<path>: one file"
      port: "http: only this port. databases: the server port"
      http_port: "clickhouse: HTTP port, default 8123"
      container: "only this docker container, by name or ID"
      reason: "trace drop: only these reasons, comma separated"
      device: "trace io: block device major:minor"
      signal: "trace exec: signals to record, names, all, or none"
      syscall: "trace syscall: only these calls, comma-separated"
      errors: "trace syscall: failed calls, all or errno names"
      files: "trace syscall: file table. On by default; with --slow or --errors it needs --files"
      no_files: "trace syscall: leave out the file table"
      all: "trace syscall: show every row of the tables, not only the first rows"
      denied: "trace priv: only denied capability checks"
      frequency: "trace cpu: samples per second per CPU, default 99"
      folded: "trace cpu: write folded stacks for a flame graph"
      lock_kind: "trace lock: kernel or futex waits only"
      off_cpu: "trace cpu: time that threads sleep, by stack"
    notes:
      - "The default output opens a full-screen trace view in a terminal."
      - "Use / to filter process, destination, event, or source text."
      - "Press s, t, p, c, or e for source, target, port, process, or event rows."
      - "Press g to scroll events."
      - "In the event list, press Up or Down to select an event. The list stops."
      - "Enter shows all fields and the whole payload. l or Esc follows again."
      - "trace syscall counts in the kernel. On a terminal it redraws the table every second, and it prints the final table on Ctrl-C."
      - "trace syscall -- <command> runs the command and counts its calls, including the processes it starts, until it exits. It returns the exit code of the command."
      - "trace syscall also lists the files that the process opened, wrote, deleted, renamed, or looked for and did not find. The rows with changes come first. --no-files turns the list off, and --all shows every row."
      - "trace syscall keeps an event when a condition holds for 5 seconds: the same call fails 100 times a second (error loop), calls on one path fail with ENOENT or ENOTDIR 50 times a second (missing path), or one call jumps to 10 times its usual rate (call spike)."
      - "trace syscall --process takes PIDs or exact command names, 15 bytes max."
      - "trace priv shows capability checks, uid and gid changes, and module loads."

- "trace reclaim counts the time that tasks wait for memory reclaim."
      - "trace cpu samples the stacks on each CPU and prints the hot functions."
      - "trace lock shows kernel lock contention and futex waits by address."
      - "Press f to follow the newest event in the detail view."
      - "Press i to show a preview under the list. J and K scroll it."
      - "trace http: v shows payload lines, m shows secrets, z decodes gzip."
      - "Press Tab for the next view and Shift+Tab for the previous view."
      - "Use --group-by source, target, port, process, or event for grouped rows."
      - "trace http also groups by path. Press u, or use --group-by path."
      - "trace io groups rows by device, process, cgroup, or event."
      - "trace io --slow sets the minimum request latency. The default is 1ms."
      - "trace sched --slow sets the minimum span latency. The default is 1ms."
      - "trace exec shows exec, exit, signal, and oom events. --signal picks signals."
      - "trace show <raw.jsonl> prints the summary of a saved --raw file, without root."
      - "--slow needs a unit, such as 20us, 500us, or 2ms. A bare number fails."
      - "Grouped rows label the event count rate EVENT/s and show payload traffic."
      - "B/s is a byte rate. bps and Mbps are bit rates. Mbps is bps / 1,000,000."
      - "Press Ctrl-C to stop a trace without --duration."
      - "Use --raw for JSONL events."
      - "--container shows the events of one docker container on Linux."
      - "The summary groups rows by process and peer. -d lists each connection."
      - "trace dns shows DNS queries and answers on Linux. It has no port view."
      - "trace arp shows neighbor table changes on Linux and macOS. It needs no root."
      - "trace ndp does the same for IPv6 neighbors."
      - "trace http reads HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2 on both sides on Linux 5.15 or later."
      - "trace http shows both sides. Each row starts with client: or server:."
      - "client: this host sent the request. server: a local server received it."
      - "--side client or --side server keeps one side. trace dns shows client."
      - "A proxy shows one request as server: from the user and client: to the backend."

      - "Its payload is raw and not hidden. In the full screen, press v to show it."

      title: "추이와 증가량"
      notes:
        - "`edc history trend`는 DB 지표를 로컬 시간·일·주 단위로 묶습니다. `edc history growth`는 디스크·디렉터리 또는 process RSS 증가량을 봅니다 (기본 7일)."
        - "process는 `--process <filter>`로 좁힙니다. 필터 없이 저장한 process는 관측된 후보이며, host CPU%는 전체 코어 기준이고 process 100%는 한 코어입니다."
    cleanup:
      title: "정리"
      notes:
        - "`edc history prune`은 마지막 활동이 `90d` 이전인 실행을 미리 봅니다. `t`로 기간 변경, `d` 다음 `y`로 체크한 실행 삭제를 확인합니다."

func parseLogOptions(args []string, stderr io.Writer) (logOptions, bool) {
	config := activeConfig.Defaults.Log
	options := logOptions{
		stream:         configuredString(config.Stream, "both"),
		output:         configuredString(config.Output, ""),
		commandDisplay: configuredString(config.CommandDisplay, "full"),
		maxSizeMB:      configuredInt(config.MaxSizeMB, defaultLogMaxSizeMB),
		keepFiles:      configuredInt(config.KeepFiles, defaultLogKeepFiles),
		restart:        configuredString(config.Restart, "never"),
		maxRestarts:    configuredInt(config.MaxRestarts, defaultLogMaxRestarts),
		restartDelay:   configuredDuration(config.RestartDelay, defaultLogRestartDelay),
		timeout:        configuredDuration(config.Timeout, 0),
		killAfter:      configuredDuration(config.KillAfter, defaultLogKillAfter),
	}
	separator := -1
	for index, argument := range args {
		if argument == "--" {
			separator = index
			break
		}
	}
	if separator < 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, T("cli.log.command_required"))
		return logOptions{}, false
	}
	set := newFlagSet("log")
	set.SetOutput(stderr)
	set.StringVar(&options.stream, "stream", options.stream, T("command.log.option.stream"))
	set.StringVar(&options.output, "output", options.output, T("command.log.option.output"))
	set.StringVar(&options.commandDisplay, "command-display", options.commandDisplay, T("command.log.option.command_display"))
	set.IntVar(&options.maxSizeMB, "max-size", options.maxSizeMB, T("command.log.option.max_size"))
	set.IntVar(&options.keepFiles, "keep-files", options.keepFiles, T("command.log.option.keep_files"))

# T1 measurement: ClickHouse native protocol write/read boundaries
# Do not edit by hand. Re-run the procedure at the end of this file to regenerate.

== Environment
- Host: OrbStack Linux VM, Ubuntu 26.04 arm64, kernel 7.0.14-orbstack, 15 CPUs. Linux only; the macOS host was not used.
- Server: clickhouse-server 26.9.16.11, tcp_port 9000 (plain), listen 127.0.0.1/::1, default config.xml, systemd unit stopped and the binary started by hand in a private UTS namespace with hostname "fixture-host" (so no real host name reaches the fixtures).
- User: <user>edc</user> with <password>edc-fixture</password> (fake) in /etc/clickhouse-server/users.d/edc.xml.
- Client: clickhouse-client 26.9.16.11, run as unix user "fixture" in a UTS namespace with hostname "fixture-host", --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000 --user edc --password edc-fixture --compression 0|1 -q "<sql>", stdout to /dev/null.
- Tracing: server: strace -f -p <pid> -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 -e trace=read,recvfrom,recvmsg,write,sendto,sendmsg,writev; client: strace -f -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 -e trace=... clickhouse-client ...
  The 2 MiB string limit keeps whole syscalls, so a packet walker could verify every boundary. Fixtures keep only the first 8192 bytes of one syscall.
- Syscalls seen: server sends with sendto, receives with recvfrom (1 MiB buffer); client the same. One syscall = one TCP send/recv record for edc.
- strace slows both processes. Timestamps are only used to order records. Record boundaries on the client read side can change with timing.
- Parser: all response bytes were walked packet by packet with a script; the walker reached the end of the stream exactly (no leftover bytes, no unknown packet) in all 16 runs on both sides (32 streams), and all 386 compressed blocks were decompressed (zstd) and parsed to the last byte with no mismatch.

== Wire facts that differ from the plan (important for T2)
1. TCP protocol revision (Hello field 5) is 54492, not the 54529 returned by revision(). Revision gating must use the Hello value. Source: ProtocolDefines.h says DBMS_TCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION is separate from VERSION_REVISION (master header shows 54494 at fetch time).
2. Native block String columns, for min(client, server) revision >= 54492 (DBMS_MIN_REVISION_WITH_STRING_WITH_SIZE_STREAM_SERIALIZATION), are NOT varuint-length-prefixed per row. Layout: UInt64 LE cumulative offsets[rows], then the concatenated characters. Row data size = 8*rows + offsets[rows-1]. The walker must read the last offset at 8*(rows-1) from the column data start. Below 54492 the old layout (varuint length per row) applies. No per-column marker exists on the wire; NativeWriter chooses the layout by revision.
   Verified: block column data for ProfileEvents (host_name, name) and Log-like repeat('x',100) blocks (65409 rows) parse to the last byte only with the offsets-first layout.
3. CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE=Memory: the server sends ONLY a 1-byte EndOfStream (0x05) after the Query. No Progress, no ProfileEvents, no Data block. So there is no ProfileEvents block for DDL to measure; server_ddl_final.hex is that single byte.
4. Query packet layout (rev 54492), offsets for "SELECT sleep(1)":
   - 0 type=1, 1 query_id (empty String 00), ClientInfo ends and settings start at offset 74, then 01 00 = external_roles (String of length 1, content 00), 00 = interserver secret (empty String), stage 02, compression 00|01, query text (length byte + text), parameters terminator 00, then empty Data block (02 00 | block) in the same write.
   - with the --compression flag the client also sends one setting: name "compression", flags 0, value "false"/"true". Query write = 130 bytes (compression 0), 163 bytes (compression 1; the trailing empty Data block is 48 bytes because it is a compressed frame). Query text length byte at offset 99 / 98, text at 100 / 99.
   - without --compression flag (default, 127.0.0.1) the Query is 104 bytes for "SELECT 1", 0 settings, text length byte at offset 80, text at 81, compression=0. A remote host default is compression=1 (not measured, E21).
   - ClientInfo: initial_user and os_user are empty strings; client_hostname = the client host name (so Query packets carry the client host name; do not print it). client_name "ClickHouse client", version 26.9, revision 54492, version_patch 16, quota_key empty, otel flag 0, client_agent empty.
5. Client Hello (41 bytes): type 0, "ClickHouse client", 26, 9, revision 54492, database "", user "edc", password "edc-fixture" at offset 29 (11 bytes). Addendum (24 bytes, no type byte): quota_key "", proto_send_chunked "notchunked", proto_recv_chunked "notchunked", parallel replicas version 8. Server Hello is 77 bytes (revision varuint at offset 14, 3 bytes), proto caps "notchunked". Hello, Addendum and Query are three separate writes.
6. Compression: default network_compression_method is ZSTD (method byte 0x90) on this server. All 386 frames-led blocks used 0x90; LZ4 (0x82) was not seen. Frames are [16 checksum][method][u32 compressed size incl 9][u32 uncompressed size].
7. Compression flag 1 compresses Data, ProfileEvents, Totals, Extremes blocks (not the packet type byte or the table-name String). ProfileEvents blocks were compressed frames (rev >= 54481 confirmed). Log packets were not observed (send_logs_level default).
8. ProfileEvents block (uncompressed): 6 columns host_name:String, current_time:DateTime, thread_id:UInt64, type:Enum8('increment' = 1, 'gauge' = 2), name:String, value:Int64. Table-name String is empty. Rows depend on query and thread count (this VM has 15 CPUs): final block 1544 bytes (39 rows, SELECT sleep), 2807 (repeat), 1384 (numbers), 2376 (32 rows, aggregation), 3494 (totals), 2868 (extremes). Compressed equivalents: 566, 939, 588, 768, 1029, 929 bytes.
9. Exception packet: type 2, Int32 LE code 60, String "DB::Exception", String message (104 bytes, ends at offset 124), String stack trace (2990 bytes), UInt8 has_nested 0. Whole Exception is one 3117-byte write; there is no EndOfStream after it.
10. The first server record after Hello is the empty header Data block (29..39 bytes uncompressed, 63..73 compressed). In SELECT sleep(1) each ~100 ms record starts with Progress (03) followed by ProfileEvents (0e).

repeat b: 3 Data blocks (of 7) used 7 frames each: usz [1048576 x6, 772755]; the frame with usz 772755 < 1048576 closed the block. Decompressing the frames and parsing them as one Native block consumed exactly 7064211 of 7064211 bytes (rows=65409, cols=1). No mismatch in any of the 386 compressed blocks of all runs. Not measured: a block whose uncompressed size is exactly 1048576 bytes (the rule would then expect another frame).

== Branch decision for T4: (b), with a documented (c) limit
(a) is rejected: server-side EndOfStream is outside the first 1024 bytes of the final write in 9 cases: uncompressed sleep 1589, numbers 1441, repeat 2860, totals 3588, extremes 2958, aggregation 2427; compressed repeat 1026, totals 1191, extremes 1087; the client sees the same offsets whenever its final read starts at the same boundary.
(b) applies: for every case above the EndOfStream offset is inside 4096 and all packets before it can be walked from the first 4096 bytes (walker check: walk-ok at 4096, walk-FAIL at 1024 for these cases). Largest measured offset: 3588 (totals, uncompressed). Raise the BPF response capture limit to 4096 for the clickhouse protocol only.
(c) still applies to:
 - client reads of large uncompressed results where the final read starts in the middle of Data (numbers a: EndOfStream@68296, repeat a: @907322). The completion cannot be seen within 4096 bytes and cannot be inferred from the first byte. Document as a limit; the server side still sees the final write.
 - servers with many threads or heavy queries: the uncompressed ProfileEvents block grows with the number of threads and counters (1384 to 3494 bytes here on 15 CPUs); a final uncompressed write above 4096 bytes is possible and was not measured. With compression 1 the block stays below 1100 bytes here.
 - uncompressed ProfileEvents walking needs the String offsets (fact 2); at revision < 54492 the old layout would apply (not measured, different server version).

== Environment

This is the same path as production: app container to ClickHouse container, container IP, no docker-proxy.

Client tracing: strace -f -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 with the same -e list in front of the command. Only syscalls on the HTTP socket (server: local port 8123, client: peer port 8123) are kept.
- Syscalls seen: sendto and recvfrom only (curl, python http.client, ClickHouse). One syscall = one record, which is what the BPF hook sees as one tcp_sendmsg/tcp_recvmsg (stage 1 relied on the same equality). TCP segment boundaries were not measured.
- strace slows both sides. Timestamps order records and give rough latencies, they are not benchmarks. Client read boundaries depend on the client and on timing.
- Defaults seen on both servers (system.settings): enable_http_compression=1, http_response_buffer_size=0, async_insert=1, wait_for_async_insert=1, async_insert_use_adaptive_busy_timeout=1, async_insert_busy_timeout_min_ms=50, async_insert_busy_timeout_max_ms=200, http_max_uri_size=1048576, http_max_field_value_size=131072. network_compression_method: LZ4 on 26.3; the compression frames seen on the 26.9 server start with method byte 0x90 (ZSTD), on 26.3 with 0x82 (LZ4).
- Reader clients: curl reads with a 102400-byte buffer. Python http.client reads through a buffered reader (reads of 2 to 338832 bytes seen). The real production client (clickhouse-rs 0.15.1, Rust) was not run; its User-Agent and header set were copied into curl (rs_insert, rs_select, rs_select_midstream_error). Whether clickhouse-rs sends the same bytes is 추정.

== Fixture format
- One file per scenario: http/<scenario>.records. Sections start with a "# version: <version> deb|docker <digest>" line. Replay each section on its own. A section can hold several runs ("# run <n>: <label>", "# command: <command>"); each run is one or more connections in time order.
- Record line: "<server|client> <send|recv> <total bytes> <hex>". hex = first min(total,4096) bytes. Client and server lines are interleaved by syscall time: filter by side. A client send equals a server recv byte for byte (checked), a server send equals a client recv.
- Deviation from "first 4096 bytes": when total > 4096 and no framing element (status line, header line, chunk size line, chunk CRLF, terminal chunk) and no "__exception__" marker starts between byte 56 and byte 4096 of the record, the hex holds only the first 64 bytes. The omitted bytes are plain chunk data or request body. T3 pads the hex with 'x' up to min(total,4096) bytes. Such padding cannot create a fake CRLF. A loader must not assume len(hex)/2 == min(total,4096).
- Lines are not wrapped, a line can be 8 KB.
- 'DATA/' in a command line means /tmp/ch/data/ on the VM (files made by "m.py data").

== Table legend
element names in "pattern=[...]" (one token per record, "|" separates records, "xN" repeats the same record kind N times, "+" joins elements that start in the same record, "~" prefix = the record starts in the middle of an element):
  st = status line, h = one header line (hxN = N header lines), he = blank line that ends the headers, csz = chunk size line, data = chunk data, crlf = CRLF after chunk data, last = terminal chunk "0 CRLF CRLF" (5 bytes), rl = request line, body = Content-Length body.
"rec<i>@<o>/<n>" = record index i (0-based, in the connection and direction), offset o in the record, record size n. "in4096=True" = the element ends inside the first 4096 bytes of that record. "alone5=True" = the terminal chunk is a record of its own with exactly 5 bytes. "walk4096" = result of walking status line, headers, chunk sizes and the terminal chunk with only the first 4096 bytes of every record visible (OK, or LOST(reason)). "walk4096_ok" is the same for requests. Times are strace start-of-call stamps relative to the first client send.
A server connection is shown as "server send" (response) and "server recv" (request); the client side as "client recv" and "client send".

== Findings that differ from the plan or add to it (for T2/T3)
1. Header block is NOT one send. The server sends the status line (17 bytes for 200 OK, 24 for 404, 36 for 500; 25 bytes for "100 Continue"), then the 22 bytes "X-ClickHouse-Summary: ", then the JSON value (183-210 bytes), then CRLF (2 bytes), then all remaining headers in one send (537-688 bytes), and for a HEAD /ping the status line and the headers (211-234 bytes) are two sends. The header end is at most 688 bytes into its record (largest over all runs). The headers never span the 4096 limit.
2. Body framing on the server: chunk size line (3-8 bytes), chunk data, CRLF (2 bytes), each as its own send; the terminal chunk "0 CRLF CRLF" is its own 5-byte send in 31 of 31 chunked responses that complete, on both versions. Chunk data sends are up to 1048576 bytes (plain results and gzip/compress=1) or 130818 bytes (throwIf test).

3. Error before the first output byte (SELECT * FROM missing_table, 404; throwIf before the first flush, 500): normal chunked response with the error text as one chunk, X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code in the headers, terminal chunk present.
4. Error after output started (HTTP status stays 200): the exception block is one chunk of its own, 365-366 bytes, sent as one send after its 5-byte chunk size line, then a 2-byte CRLF send. Layout: "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag 16 letters>\r\n<message>\n<message length> <tag>\r\n__exception__\r\n". The tag equals the X-ClickHouse-Exception-Tag header. The marker "__exception__" appears twice but only the first one is followed by the tag. NO terminal chunk follows: the server closes the connection (curl exit code 18, client recv returned 0).
5. The server closes the connection after a mid-stream error and after an HTTP/1.0 response; for HTTP/1.0 (curl --http1.0) the response is "HTTP/1.0 200 OK" with "Connection: Close" and no Content-Length and no chunking, so the body end is only the close.
6. "Expect: 100-continue" (curl, 2 MiB POST): the server sends "HTTP/1.1 100 Continue" as its own 25-byte send 2.4 ms (26.9) / 2.8 ms (26.3) after the request headers, then reads the body, then sends the final response. The upload took about 19 ms (26.9) / 29 ms (26.3) under strace. The server recv splits the body into 7 (26.9) or 9 (26.3) records.
7. Chunked request (python encode_chunked, and curl "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" in rs_insert): the client sends headers and chunks in separate sends or in one send, the server recv coalesces them (chunked_request: client 5 sends, server 1 recv of 269/270 bytes). In rs_insert (curl, 5166 byte LZ4 frame) the headers (233 bytes) and the whole chunked body are ONE send/recv of 5412 bytes; the chunk size line is at offset 233, the chunk data is 5166 bytes, and the chunk CRLF and the terminal chunk are the last 7 bytes of the same record, past byte 4096, so the request walk with 4096 bytes cannot reach the end of the request (walk4096_ok=False).

9. Default query SQL rules verified through system.query_log on both versions (query_ids edc-t1-plus, edc-t1-body, edc-t1-post, edc-t1-dup): '+' in the URL query parameter becomes a space and %2B becomes '+' (SELECT 1 AS a, 'p+q' AS b, 'x y'); with a body the text is "<query parameter>\n<body>" (query=SELECT 42 and body " FORMAT JSONCompact" gave "SELECT 42\n FORMAT JSONCompact"); a query parameter with no body still gets a trailing "\n"; with a repeated query parameter only the first is used; without the parameter the body is the whole SQL.

11. clickhouse-compressor --codec LZ4 output was accepted by "decompress=1" on both versions (1000 RowBinary rows inserted, count checked). Whether it matches clickhouse-rs bytes is 추정.
12. Records of the same response read by curl: for results up to a few KB the client reads mirror the server sends (some adjacent small sends are merged, for example "csz+data" as one 5-byte read). For results of 64 KB and more curl reads 56 to 102400 bytes and most reads start in the middle of chunk data (big: 778 reads on 26.9 for 465 server sends).

== A1..A9 verdicts
A1 (server send unit, terminal chunk separate): CONFIRMED on 26.9 and 26.3. Every one of the 31 completed chunked responses per version ends with a lone 5-byte record at offset 0; the sends are: status line, "X-ClickHouse-Summary: ", JSON, CRLF, other headers, size line, data, CRLF, ..., terminal chunk (finding 1 and 2). Sizes differ only by the version string and header count. TCP segmentation was not measured, so a BPF record = one send is the assumption stated in Environment.
A2 (client reads mix): CONFIRMED and client dependent. curl: small results mirror the server; big, wait_end, gzip and compress=1 results of 18 KB and more put the chunk size lines and the terminal chunk inside reads of 18-95 KB (see table, tail lines). Python http.client on big: 439 reads (26.9) / 414 (26.3), last read is the lone 5-byte terminal chunk but the chunk size lines in between are beyond 4096 of their records, so the walk is lost anyway.
A3 (container network): PARTLY CONFIRMED. Direct path from edc-client (172.18.0.3) to edc-ch263 (172.18.0.2:8123): the server socket is 172.18.0.2:8123 <-> 172.18.0.3:<port>, the client socket sits in the client container network namespace, and docker-proxy shows no socket activity at all during the request. Published path (host curl to 127.0.0.1:18123): TWO sockets: client <-> docker-proxy (127.0.0.1:18123) and docker-proxy <-> server (172.18.0.1:<port> -> 172.18.0.2:8123), so the server sees peer 172.18.0.1. docker-proxy moves the bytes with splice(2) (socket -> pipe -> socket), not with recv/send. NOT TESTED in T1: whether the kernel hooks of edc see the sockets in the container network namespaces (strace only); the splice path is relevant for T7.
A4 (pipelining): PARTLY REFUTED. Two requests in ONE send (one 354-byte recv on the server): only the first is answered; the second got no response within 4 s, on both versions (python pipe_one). Two requests in two sends before the first response (sleep(1) request, then SELECT 2 50 ms later): both answered in order, the second response starts about 7 ms after the first ends (pipe_two). So a FIFO in T3 gets a permanent unanswered entry in the first case. /ping and queries on one keep-alive connection work in order (keepalive_ping run 0).
A5 (compressed mid-stream error): PARTLY REFUTED, see the compress=1 verdict. gzip (Accept-Encoding + enable_http_compression): 0 of 2 versions show the marker.
A6 (async insert): CONFIRMED. Both servers have async_insert=1 and wait_for_async_insert=1 for user edc. async_wait1: first response record +77.1 ms (26.9) / +75.5 ms (26.3), the Summary elapsed_ns is 72.7 / 71.2 ms. async_wait0: +6.7 ms / +12.2 ms. The flush came at about 75 ms, not at the 200 ms busy timeout; async_insert_use_adaptive_busy_timeout=1 with min 50 ms and max 200 ms is the likely reason (추정). A plain insert without the async parameters (insert_format +81.6 ms, insert_values +84.1 ms to the first response record on 26.9) behaves like wait=1, as the defaults say.
A7 (docker): docker.io installed on the VM with user approval; the 26.3 image was used, no tgz fallback.
A8 (request line and headers within 4096): CONFIRMED for normal requests (the largest request header block measured: 289 bytes, curl/python/clickhouse-rs shapes) and measured for a 5 KB URL (finding 8): the SQL is cut at 4096 bytes, the header end is not visible, the request walk is lost, the response is fine. The next request on the same connection (server side) was not measured.
A9: a decision, not measurable.
Other checks: "X-ClickHouse-Summary elapsed_ns" is the value at the first header flush: sleep(1) 1007.7 / 1009.5 ms (the headers are flushed after the query finished) vs big 7.5 / 5.7 ms while the terminal chunk arrived at +417.8 / +396.9 ms (strace). So elapsed_ns must not be used for latency (agrees with the plan). Request-to-terminal-chunk times: small +14.6 / +13.4 ms, sleep +1017.3 / +1021.7 ms, error +6.6 / +23.4 ms, wait_end +52.7 / +62.9 ms (26.9 / 26.3).

== Branch decisions
S: (S-a) holds. The server-side chunk walk with only the first 4096 bytes of each record reaches the end of every response that has an end: 33 of 41 server responses per version ("walk4096=OK"; 31 chunked with the lone 5-byte terminal chunk, 1 HEAD, 1 100-continue interim). The other 8 per version (http10, midstream x2, midstream_gzip run 2, rs_select_midstream_error runs 1-4) are not walk failures: the stream simply has no terminal chunk and no framing end (exception then close, or HTTP/1.0 close), which is the E and unanswered case. The largest header block end is at offset 688 (26.9) / 662 (26.3) of its record.
C: (C-b). The plan's condition is not met: (1) The last client read is "0 CRLF CRLF" as a lone 5-byte record in most runs, not the 7-byte form "CRLF 0 CRLF CRLF" the plan names (the 7-byte form shows up only when the last read also holds chunk data, or in compress1 on 26.9). (2) Of the 33 client connections per version, the last read is the tail and at most 4096 bytes in 22 (26.9) / 23 (26.3). In 5 (26.9: curl big 17689 bytes, gzip 19339, midstream_gzip run 1 4142 (46 bytes over the limit), rs_select 25842, wait_end 18499) / 4 (26.3: big 59689, gzip 71670, rs_select 21389, wait_end 94988) the last read ends with the tail but is bigger than 4096 bytes, with the tail at offset 4137 to 94983; the BPF record keeps only the first 4096 bytes, so the tail cannot be seen there. In 6 / 6 there is no tail at the end (HEAD, HTTP/1.0, mid-stream errors). (3) The tail would rescue only one client response whose chunk walk was lost (python http.client big: lone 5-byte record at the end); the other 5 (26.9) / 4 (26.3) lost-sync client responses (curl big, gzip, rs_select, wait_end, and on 26.9 midstream_gzip run 1) end in a record the tail is invisible in. (4) No data read that is not the last read of its response ended with the tail or equalled the 5-byte tail in any run (keepalive_ping hits are the real ends of the earlier responses). So the rule would have been safe (0 false positives in 66 connections), but it saves 1 of 6 / 1 of 5 cases, and the plan says the condition must hold for small/error/compressed results with the 7-byte form. T3: no tail inference; a client response whose walk is lost is "unanswered". The server-side event of the same query still has the end and the latency.
E: (E-a) for the server side and for client reads that keep up; (E-b) for the rest. Uncompressed mid-stream error: the "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag>" marker is at offset 2 of a dedicated 365/366-byte record on the server in all 4 runs (26.9 and 26.3, two midstream runs each) and the tag equals the header tag. On the client the marker is at offset 2 of its own record for curl (2 of 2 runs, one per version). The slow python reader on 26.9 got it at offset 657295 of a 657661-byte read (outside 4096); on 26.3 the same slow reader still read it as its own 365-byte record at offset 2. So the client side is E-a only when the reader keeps up; a coalesced read is E-b (unanswered). The marker detection must also require the tag from the X-ClickHouse-Exception-Tag header (finding 4), because "__exception__" alone can be data.
compress=1 verdict (the clickhouse-rs shape: POST, Content-Length, compress=1, default_format=RowBinary; rs_select, rs_select_midstream_error):
  - Normal answer: status line, headers, chunks, lone 5-byte terminal chunk on the server (31/31); the completion is the terminal chunk and the server-side latency is correct. The client side cannot see it when the last read is above 4096 (rs_select: 25842 bytes on 26.9, 21389 on 26.3).
  - Error before the first flush (throwIf with compressible output, runs 0): 500 status, X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code in the headers, one body chunk (1323 bytes on 26.9, 7567 on 26.3), terminal chunk present -> normal completion plus exception from the status and header, both versions.
  - Error after output started (runs 1-4: incompressible rows): the status stays 200, there is no terminal chunk, the server closes the connection. The marker "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag>" is visible on 26.3 (LZ4 frame, the text stays as literal bytes): server record offset 29 of a 313-, 313-, 297- and 350-byte record in 4 of 4 runs, tag equals the header tag; but the message after it is back-referenced and unreadable. On 26.9 (ZSTD frame) the marker is not visible in 0 of 4 runs. The same holds for gzip (Accept-Encoding: gzip with enable_http_compression=1): marker not visible, no terminal chunk, server closes.
  - Decision: detect with the same rule as E-a on any record (marker + tag from the header inside the first 4096 bytes); it works by accident on 26.3 + LZ4 (production: 26.3), it never works on 26.9 + ZSTD or gzip, so a mid-stream error with compression is "unanswered" unless the marker happens to be visible. On the client side the 26.3 marker was always inside a large read, at offset 74250, 52101, 43094 and 65198 (4 of 4 runs), never in the first 4096 bytes, so a compressed mid-stream error is unanswered on the client side.

A5 therefore changes from "never visible" to "visible only with LZ4 on 26.3, not guaranteed".

LINE = re.compile(r'^(?:\[pid\s+(\d+)\]\s*|(\d+)\s+)?(\d+\.\d+)\s+(.*)$')
RES = re.compile(r'^<\.\.\. (\w+) resumed>(.*)$')
FD = re.compile(r'^(\w+)\((\d+)<TCP:\[(.*?)\]>')

def addr(s):
    h, p = s.rsplit(':', 1)
    return h.strip('[]'), int(p)

def parse_strace(path, side, port):
    recs = []; pend = {}; seen = set()
    with open(path, 'r', errors='replace') as f:
        for line in f:
            m = LINE.match(line.rstrip('\n'))
            if not m: continue
            pid = m.group(1) or m.group(2); ts = float(m.group(3)); rest = m.group(4)
            if rest.startswith('<... '):
                m2 = RES.match(rest)
                if not m2: continue
                p = pend.pop(pid, None)
                if p is None: continue

== Deviations from the plan (T1 Definition of Done)
1. PGDG resolute-pgdg was not usable. The VM is Ubuntu 25.04 (plucky, glibc 2.41), not 26.04. The resolute-pgdg postgresql-16 package needs libc6 >= 2.43. The plucky-pgdg suite was moved to apt-archive.postgresql.org and holds amd64 only. So the PGDG noble-pgdg (Ubuntu 24.04, needs libc6 >= 2.38) arm64 packages postgresql-16, postgresql-client-16 and libpq5, plus libicu74 from ports.ubuntu.com noble-updates, were unpacked with dpkg-deb -x into /tmp/edc-pg/root and run from there with LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Nothing was installed system wide (no apt-get install, no dpkg -i). The major version is 16 as required.
2. The VM was not stopped at the end. The ubuntu VM is shared with other agents that run at the same time, and the batch rules forbid stopping or restarting it. The server was stopped (pg_ctl stop -m fast) and /tmp/edc-pg was removed instead.
3. gssenc_refused: the PGDG build has GSSAPI, and PostgreSQL 16 answers 'G' to a GSSENCRequest on any TCP socket, with or without a keytab (ProcessStartupPacket: gss = 'G' unless the socket is AF_UNIX). An 'N' answer over TCP needs a build without GSSAPI. The fixture therefore has two runs: run 0 = TCP, GSSENCRequest, 'G', client closes (no Kerberos credentials). Run 1 = the same server over its Unix socket, GSSENCRequest, 'N', plain StartupMessage, SCRAM, SELECT 1, Terminate. The run 1 bytes are the bytes a non-GSSAPI server sends over TCP; only the transport differs. libpq itself sends GSSENCRequest only when it finds Kerberos credentials (libpq documentation for gssencmode=prefer); psql in this environment never sent one.
4. pipeline: pgbench 16 has \startpipeline and \endpipeline but no \syncpipeline (added in 17), so one pgbench pipeline is one Sync batch. Several Sync batches before the first ReadyForQuery come from the raw-socket harness (pipeline run 1).
5. The extended scenario uses all three named options: psql 16 \bind (unnamed statement), pgbench -M prepared (named statement P_0), and the raw-socket harness (named statement edc_stmt, named portals edc_portal and edc_cursor, Execute with a row limit, Close, FunctionCall).
6. large: the fixture file holds the N=1e3 run in full. The N=1e5, N=1e6 and generate_series(1,1e6) runs are 11 MB, 111 MB and 17 MB per direction, so the fixture keeps only their tail (see "Fixture format"). Their measurements below use every record.
7. Extra runs not named in the plan: simple run 1 (CancelRequest on a second connection while SELECT pg_sleep(5) runs) and error run 0 also has a division by zero after 499 DataRows (error in the middle of a result).
8. copy_extended was added after a review, in a second capture on the same VM with the same setup: "m.py fetch; m.py setup; m.py run copy_extended". == Fixture format
- One file per scenario: <scenario>.records. A file has one section: "# version: 16.15 (SHOW server_version: ...)". A section holds runs; "# run <n>: <label>" starts a run and "# command: <command>" names the client command (W/ = /tmp/edc-pg/ on the VM; m.py = the script at the end of this file). One run is one connection (TCP unless the label says Unix socket): replay each run with a new tracker and a new socket id. A client command that opened two connections (pgbench, cancel) becomes two runs with "[connection i of n]" in the label.
- Record line: "<server|client> <send|recv> <total bytes> <hex>". hex = the first min(total,16384) bytes of the record. Client and server lines are interleaved by syscall time: filter by side. In every run except ssl, client send equals server recv byte for byte and server send equals client recv byte for byte (checked over the whole connection). ssl: each side's last 24-byte TLS alert (close_notify) was not read by the peer before it closed.
- "# tail-only:" (large runs 1-3): the first records of the connection (startup, query, head of the result) are omitted. The run keeps every record, on both sides, from the earlier of the second-to-last server send and the second-to-last client recv. The tracker sees the connection for the first time at the first kept record, in the middle of a DataRow stream, and the request that started the result is not in the run.
- Records are never longer than 16384 bytes in these captures (server sends <= 8192, libpq reads <= 16384), so every hex field holds the whole record. To test truncation (captured < size), cut the hex in the test.
- Lines are not wrapped. A line can be 32 KB.

== Re-run procedure (Linux VM, arm64, port 5432 free, sudo for strace -p)
1. orb start ubuntu (if it is stopped). In the VM: mkdir -p /tmp/edc-pg, then extract the script: sed -n '/^%%BEGIN m.py/,/^%%END m.py/p' boundaries.txt | sed '1d;$d' > /tmp/edc-pg/m.py
2. python3 /tmp/edc-pg/m.py fetch: downloads the newest postgresql-16, postgresql-client-16 and libpq5 from noble-pgdg arm64 and libicu74 from ports.ubuntu.com, and unpacks them into /tmp/edc-pg/root (no system install). Needs curl, dpkg-deb, openssl, strace and python3 on the VM.
3. python3 /tmp/edc-pg/m.py setup: certificate, initdb, configuration (see Environment), server start, role edc, database edc, tables t and u.
4. python3 /tmp/edc-pg/m.py run all (about 1.5 minutes; one scenario: "run simple", several: comma separated). Each run sets pg_hba and ssl, prepares the tables, attaches strace to the postmaster, runs the client under strace, then reduces the raw strace output to /tmp/edc-pg/red/<scenario>.<run>.json and deletes it (the 1e6 runs write about 1 GB of raw strace text to /tmp for a few seconds).
5. python3 /tmp/edc-pg/m.py assemble /tmp/edc-pg/out: writes out/<scenario>.records (the fixtures) and out/analysis.txt (the per-scenario table of this file).
6. Copy out/*.records into internal/edc/testdata/postgres/, replace the per-scenario table and the large result summary in this file, and run the grep of "Secrets and host names" again.
7. python3 /tmp/edc-pg/m.py clean: stops the server and removes /tmp/edc-pg. Do not stop a VM that other people use.
A re-run gets a newer 16.x when PGDG publishes one; the server send sizes depend on PqSendBuffer (8192) and not on the minor version (추정, not tested with another minor version).

Grep (decode the hex, then grep), run in internal/edc/testdata/postgres:
dec() { grep -v '^#' "$1" | cut -d' ' -f4 | tr -d '\n' | xxd -r -p; }
for f in *.records; do for v in edc-fixture edc-literal-secret edc-detail-secret edc-param-secret edc-copy-secret edc-func-secret ',p='; do dec $f | grep -a -o -- "$v" | wc -l; done; done
Counts (each value is counted on both sides, so a message seen once is counted 2 times):
- edc-fixture (the role password): startup_cleartext 2 = one PasswordMessage. Every other fixture: 0 in the data. The "# command:" comment lines of all files carry PGPASSWORD=edc-fixture (fake).
- SCRAM client-final-message "c=biws,r=<nonce>,p=<proof>" (SASLResponse) and SASLInitialResponse "n,,n=,r=<nonce>": startup_scram 2, simple 4, error 2, extended 8, pipeline 6, copy 2, large 2 (run 0 only, the tail-only runs have no startup), ssl_refused 2, gssenc_refused 2 (run 1), copy_extended 4. AuthenticationSASLContinue (salt, iteration count 4096, server nonce) and AuthenticationSASLFinal (server signature) are in the same fixtures.
- edc-literal-secret: simple 4 = the Query text and the DataRow value.
- edc-detail-secret: error 6 = two Query texts and one ErrorResponse D field "Key (v)=(edc-detail-secret) already exists.".
- edc-param-secret: extended 12 = Bind parameter values (psql \bind 1, pgbench -M prepared 2, harness 2) plus one DataRow (psql: SELECT $1::text echoes the value).
- edc-copy-secret: copy 4 = one CopyData from the client (COPY FROM STDIN) and one CopyData from the server (COPY TO STDOUT). copy_extended 4 = one client CopyData in each of the 2 runs.
- edc-func-secret: extended 2 = the FunctionCall argument.
- BackendKeyData (process id and cancel key) is in every plain startup answer. CancelRequest with the same key: simple run 1, connection 2.

== Environment
- Host: OrbStack Linux VM "ubuntu", Ubuntu 25.04 arm64, kernel 7.0.14-orbstack, 9 CPUs. Linux only; nothing was installed on the macOS host.
- Packages installed in the VM with apt: redis-server and redis-tools 5:7.0.15-3ubuntu0.1, strace 6.14-0ubuntu1. The redis-server systemd unit was stopped and disabled right after the install; it never served a fixture.
- The VM is shared with other work, so it was started with "orb start ubuntu" when needed and NOT stopped afterwards (deviation from the plan, which asked for "orb stop ubuntu"). All files of this capture lived under /tmp/edc-redis in the VM and were removed at the end.
- Server: started by hand for every scenario (fresh process, empty data set) in a private UTS namespace with hostname fixture-host:
  sudo unshare --uts sh -c "hostname fixture-host; exec redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6379 --requirepass edc-fixture-pass --enable-debug-command local --save '' --appendonly no --dir /tmp/edc-redis/data --logfile /tmp/edc-redis/out/server.log --daemonize no"
  The host name does not show up in any captured byte (RESP traffic carries no host name in these scenarios).
- Clients ran in the VM and connected to 127.0.0.1:6379: redis-benchmark and redis-cli 7.0.15 (hiredis, 16384-byte reads), OpenBSD netcat 1.228 (inline), and /tmp/edc-redis/bin/client.py (Python 3.13 raw sockets, TCP_NODELAY, recv(16384) like hiredis, one sendall per step) for the scenarios that need two connections in a fixed order or replies with no fixed count.
- Server tracing: sudo strace -f -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 -e trace=read,recvfrom,recvmsg,readv,write,sendto,sendmsg,writev -p <redis-server pid> -o <scenario>.server.st (attached 1 s before the client started, detached 0.5 s after it ended).
- Client tracing: strace -f -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 -e trace=read,recvfrom,recvmsg,readv,write,sendto,sendmsg,writev -o <scenario>.client.st sh -c "<command>".
- Only syscalls on a TCP socket with local port 6379 (server) or peer port 6379 (client) and a positive return value are kept. Calls returning -1 EAGAIN and 0 (EOF) are dropped. For writev/readv the iov_base strings are joined and cut to the return value.
- strace slows both sides. Timestamps order the records; they are not benchmarks.

== Fixture format
- One file per scenario: <scenario>.records. Same format as ../clickhouse/http/*.records: header comments, then one section that starts at "# version: Redis server v=7.0.15 (Ubuntu apt redis-server 5:7.0.15-3ubuntu0.1 arm64)". Replay each section on its own.
- Inside the section, every "# run <n>: <title>, <role>" starts one TCP connection, followed by "# command: <client command line>". Runs are in the order of the first record of each connection. Connections of one scenario were open at the same time (for example subscriber and publisher); their relative order is in the step logs below, not in the file.
- Record line: "<server|client> <send|recv> <total bytes> <hex>". hex = exactly the first min(total,4096) bytes (no 64-byte shortening as in the ClickHouse HTTP fixtures, so len(hex)/2 == min(total,4096) always holds). One line per syscall, server and client lines interleaved by syscall time: filter by side.
- server recv = request bytes read by redis-server, server send = reply bytes written by redis-server, client send = request bytes written by the client, client recv = reply bytes read by the client. Per connection, the server recv byte stream equals the client send stream and the server send stream equals the client recv stream (checked by the analysis: same frame lists); the record boundaries differ on the two sides.
- One syscall = one record, which is what the BPF hook sees as one tcp_sendmsg/tcp_recvmsg (the same assumption as the ClickHouse fixtures). TCP segment boundaries were not measured.
- Paths "in/..." in command lines are relative to /tmp/edc-redis in the VM.
